title: The Word's Incarnation and Iconicity
english: If the Word has taken the beginning of generation, having passed through a mother's womb to carry bodily harmonies, it is established that he became from a woman. But if the Word was God from above with the Father, and we say that all things came through him, then he who is was not become from a woman, being the cause of all those who are born; rather the nature of God is self-sufficient, infinite, and unsearchable; but from a woman a man became, having been frozen in the Holy Spirit in the virgin womb.

For the pure and spotless one is truly a temple, and the tabernacle according to man concerning the Word, where God has clearly pitched his tent. And we do not say these things from images; for he, the Son of the nature of God, announcing the release and resurrection of the new, is undoubtedly supplying and teaching us, saying to the hybrid Jews: 'destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up' (John 2:19). Thus the Word, having worked the man as a sailor, while visiting men in body, was showing all kinds of unseen miracles, and he sent out the apostles as heralds of the eternal kingdom.

For Paul did not say 'conformed to the form of the Son of God', but 'conformed to the image of his Son', showing something else regarding the Son being, and something else regarding his image. For the Son, bringing the recognitions of the divine attributes of the Father, is an icon of the Father; since also being born similar from similar ones, those giving birth appear to be true icons of the begetters. But the man whom he carried is an icon of the Son, who is even sketched as an image of colors from dissimilar ones; some being hand-made positions, others having come to be by nature and likeness. Furthermore, the Truth himself teaches this by law. For the incorporeal Spirit of Wisdom is not conformed to bodily men, but the man having been embodied by the Spirit is a character, wearing equal members to all others, and having been clothed with the same idea for each.

That the body is said to be conformed to human beings, he teaches us more clearly, writing to the Philippians: 'Our citizenship is in the heavens, from which we also await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform the body of our humiliation, so as to become like the body of his glory' (Phil 3:20-21). If, then, transforming the humble body of men, he fashions it conformed to his own body, the slander of opposites is proven from every side. But just as the man, having been born from the virgin, is said to have come from a woman, so also it is written to have become under the law by means of the legal [things]...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
